source.bfsMunicipalityList: internal register data/raw/bfs_municipalities_register.csv (already present in this project, filtered to cantonCode=BE)

notes: YEAR: 2026 figures used throughout. The ESTV Kantonsblatt Bern (Stand Februar 2026) explicitly marks most of the 2026 income-tax bracket thresholds with 'Gültig ab Steuerperiode 2026' (cold-progression/kalte Progression adjustment per Art. 3 StG, applied whenever the national CPI has moved >=3% since the last adjustment), confirming 2026 is the correct, currently-enacted year, distinct from 2025 figures. The official municipal/church multiplier source is also explicitly the '...für 2026' edition (Finanzverwaltung des Kantons Bern, 'Steueranlagen der Gemeinden und Steuersätze der Kirchgemeinden für 2026', Stand 01.02.2026), downloaded 2026-09-08. SOURCES: both PDFs were fetched and saved to data/raw/sources/ (BE_kantonsblatt_estv_2026.pdf = ESTV Kantonsblatt with income/wealth tariff tables in Art. 42/44/65 StG excerpts; BE_fv_steueranlage_gemeinden_2026.pdf = 56-page official cantonal Finanzverwaltung publication with per-municipality multipliers and church rates, Table 2.2 'Reihenfolge nach Verwaltungskreisen' used as primary extraction source since it already groups every municipality under its own Verwaltungskreis heading). MECHANISM - 'JAEHRLICHES VIELFACHES' / STEUERANLAGE (genuine BE-specific quirk, important for implementation): unlike cantons that express the cantonal/municipal multiplier as a plain percentage of a Grundtarif result, Bern's Steuergesetz (Art. 2-3 StG) defines the income/wealth bracket tables above as producing the 'einfache Steuer' (simple tax) directly IN PERCENT OF INCOME (the printed tariff literally reads 'Einfache Steuer in Prozent' against 'Zu versteuerndes Einkommen' - i.e. the numbers in the bracket tables ARE the marginal tax-rate-on-income, already expressed as %, NOT a separate rate-times-bracket-then-multiply step), and wealth tax is per-mille of wealth. On top of that einfache-Steuer result, THREE independent layers each apply their OWN 'Steueranlage' - a multiplicative FACTOR ('Vielfaches der einfachen Steuer', e.g. 2.975), not a percentage - one set by the Grosser Rat (canton), one set annually by each Einwohnergemeinde (municipality, via its own budget vote), and one set annually by each Kirchgemeinde (parish, only if the taxpayer is affiliated). All three factors multiply the SAME einfache-Steuer base independently and are then summed (they are NOT chained/compounded, and NOT applied to different bases) - functionally identical in structure to a 'percent multiplier on top' mechanism, just expressed as a decimal factor (e.g. 2.975) instead of a percent number (297.5%). This dataset follows this project's established convention (e.g. GR.json) of converting all such multiplier factors to percent by multiplying by 100, so cantonalMultiplier.value=297.5 corresponds to the official 2026 cantonal Steueranlage of 2.975 for natural persons (source: Finanzverwaltung fv-stat-steueranlage_2026, section 1.2 'Kantonssteueranlagen': natural persons 2.975 / legal persons 2.620 for 2026, down from 2.975/2.620 already in 2025 - i.e. UNCHANGED between 2025 and 2026; legal persons have used a materially lower factor than natural persons since 2021, a genuine and deliberate two-track cantonal Steueranlage split introduced in 2021 that this dataset does not model since it only covers natural persons). QUIRK - GAMBLING WINNINGS EXCLUDED FROM MULTIPLIER: Art. 2 Abs. 3 Bst. a StG explicitly excludes income tax on Geldspielgewinne (gambling/lottery winnings, taxed at a flat separate 10% per Art. 45 StG) from the Steueranlage multiplier chain entirely; church tax on gambling winnings is instead a flat separate 8% of the cantonal tax on those winnings (Art. 11 Abs. 2 KStG) - a small carve-out a developer should know about but out of scope for the ordinary income/wealth bracket tables here. QUIRK - WEALTH TAX CLIFF-STYLE EXEMPTION (important, verified from Art. 65 Abs. 3 StG): 'Die Vermögenssteuer wird nicht erhoben, wenn das satzbestimmende Vermögen kleiner ist als 100'000 Franken' - i.e. wealth tax is a genuine CLIFF exemption at CHF 100'000 of rate-determining wealth, NOT simply an extension of the bracket table's own 0%-first-CHF-36'000 band. The bracket table on its own would already produce a small positive tax for wealth between CHF 36'000 and CHF 100'000 (0.4-0.7 per mille), but the separate Freigrenze in Art. 65 Abs. 3 overrides this and reduces the tax to exactly zero for ANY taxpayer whose total satzbestimmendes Vermögen is below CHF 100'000 - only once wealth reaches/exceeds CHF 100'000 does the ordinary progressive bracket table (starting from CHF 0) apply in full. A correct implementation must apply this as an if(wealth < 100000) return 0 special case layered on top of the bracket table, not just rely on the bracket table's own first two bands. QUIRK - WEALTH TAX CAP (Höchstbelastung, Art. 66 StG): total wealth tax (cantonal+municipal+church combined) is capped at 25% of net wealth-yield (Vermögensertrag) of BE-taxable assets, but never reduced below 2.4 per mille (0.0024) of taxable wealth regardless - a relief-cap mechanism not modeled in the bracket table itself; a precision implementation would need the taxpayer's actual investment income to apply it, out of scope here but flagged for developers. MARRIED-COUPLE MECHANISM: Bern does NOT use an income-splitting divisor for married couples/registered partners/single-parent families (Einelternfamilien); instead Art. 42 StG defines a wholly SEPARATE, structurally different bracket table (Art. 42 Abs. 1, 'Tarif für Verheiratete und Einelternfamilien') with its own thresholds and its own (lower) marginal rates at every bracket versus the single tariff (Art. 42 Abs. 2) - this is a genuine dual-tariff system (like Vaud/Solothurn's shape but NOT a simple multiplicative splitting divisor - the married table's breakpoints and rates were verified to NOT be a constant multiple of the single table's, ruling out a simple splitting-divisor derivation), so both tables above were transcribed directly and independently from the source rather than derived from one another. INCOME BRACKET TABLES: both tables were transcribed from the source's own cumulative 'für die ersten X / für die weiteren Y' presentation by converting each row's ending cumulative income into an absolute 'from' threshold (running sum of the CHF column) paired with that row's own marginal rate; monotonicity of the resulting cumulative tax was spot-checked and holds throughout both tables (rates rise monotonically bracket-to-bracket in both the single and married tariffs, with no drop-back quirk of the kind seen in some other cantons - BE's tariff caps out at a flat 6.5% top marginal rate for all income above CHF 470'600 single / CHF 486'000 married, and never decreases). WEALTH TAX BRACKET TABLE: transcribed the same way from Art. 65 Abs. 1 StG's cumulative per-mille table and converted per-mille to decimal (divide by 1000, per wealthTaxRateUnit=decimal); monotonicity holds strictly except for one deliberate top-end drop mirroring the income-tax cap-like shape: the marginal rate rises from 0 up to 1.35 per-mille at CHF 3'728'000-6'303'000, then DROPS to a flat 1.25 per-mille for all wealth above CHF 6'303'000 (verified directly from the source text: '1,35 für die weiteren 2'575'000' immediately followed by '1,25 für jedes weitere Vermögen') - this is a genuine, deliberate top-bracket regression similar in spirit to Solothurn's income-tax top-end drop, not a transcription error; cumulative tax remains non-decreasing throughout since no rate is negative. There is only ONE unified wealth-tax schedule for all filers (single and married use the same wealthTaxBrackets.general; BE's StG does not provide a separate married wealth-tax tariff). MUNICIPAL DATA EXTRACTION: the official 56-page PDF's Table 2.2 (grouped by the 10 Verwaltungskreise, the post-2010 administrative districts that replaced the old Amtsbezirke) was parsed with a coordinate-tolerant regex over pdftotext -layout output; this yielded exactly 334 top-level municipality rows (matching this project's existing BFS register count of 334 BE municipalities exactly, with all 334 successfully cross-matched to data/raw/bfs_municipalities_register.csv bfsNumbers after resolving ~51 abbreviation mismatches by hand, e.g. PDF 'Aeschi b. Sp.' vs BFS-register canonical 'Aeschi bei Spiez', PDF 'Büren a. A.' vs 'Büren an der Aare', PDF 'Lengnau' vs '(BE)'-suffixed BFS canonical names, etc. - the abbreviation 'b. B.' is genuinely ambiguous in the source and resolves differently per municipality (bei Büren / bei Burgdorf / bei Brienz depending on which Verwaltungskreis the row appears under), which is why matching was done manually rather than by a single automated abbreviation-expansion rule). Each municipality row carries: municipalMultiplier (Steueranlage natürliche Personen, converted factor->percent, e.g. Bern city = 154%), municipalMultiplierLegalPersons (Steueranlage juristische Personen, an EXTRA field beyond the required schema, included because in a handful of municipalities - e.g. Büetigen 1.55 vs 1.85 - the natural- and legal-person Steueranlage genuinely differ, a real quirk some cantons don't have), churchMultiplierReformed/Catholic/ChristCatholic (Kirchensteuersatz ev.-ref. / röm.-kath. / chr.-kath., converted factor->percent the same way), and provisional2026 (true for exactly 3 municipalities - Brienzwiler, Rebévelier, Attiswil - whose 2026 Anlage is footnoted '** provisorische Anlage' in the source, meaning not yet finally confirmed at publication time; flagged here in case the canton later revises these). QUIRK - SUB-MUNICIPALITY / KIRCHGEMEINDE FRAGMENTATION: 25 additional 'Unterabteilungen' (sub-divisions) appear in the source with their OWN distinct church-tax rates but no separate municipal Steueranlage of their own (they use their parent municipality's Anlage) - e.g. Petit-Val has a sub-entry 'Châtelat/Fornet-dessous' with reformed=0.3200/catholic=0.3116 vs the parent's reformed=0.3200/catholic=0.2415; Forst-Längenbühl has sub-entry 'Längenbühl' with its own church rates; Fraubrunnen has sub-entry 'Etzelkofen, Mülchi'. These reflect historical Kirchgemeinde boundaries that split a single political municipality across multiple parishes (the same phenomenon flagged for Solothurn's Buchegg/Mümliswil-Ramiswil elsewhere in this project) - BE_municipalities.json intentionally uses only each municipality's own top-level/primary row (consistent with this project's SO precedent) and does NOT separately encode the 25 Ortsteil-level sub-rates; a precision-sensitive implementation should consult BE_fv_steueranlage_gemeinden_2026.pdf Table 2.2 directly for exact per-Ortsteil church rates. CHURCH TAX STRUCTURE: BE recognizes three tax-levying Landeskirchen - evangelisch-reformiert, römisch-katholisch, and christkatholisch (an unusually widespread christ-catholic presence versus most other cantons, present in nearly every municipality here, generally in a narrow 0.23-0.306 factor/23-30.6% band) - each Kirchgemeinde sets its own annual Steueranlage exactly like a municipality does, per Art. 12 KStG; church tax for legal persons is computed as a population/tax-base-weighted average across the Kirchgemeinden touching that municipality (the source's own extra 'juristische Personen' church-tax column) and may not be levied for kultische (religious/cultic) purposes per Art. 1a KStG - this extra column was not carried into the municipality dataset since only natural-person figures are in scope. BILINGUAL NAMING: consistent with BE being officially bilingual, Verwaltungskreis names for the French-speaking Jura bernois district appear in the source as 'Arrondissement administratif Jura bernois' rather than 'Verwaltungskreis ...'; this project's existing BFS register already normalizes district names, so BE_municipalities.json uses the BFS register's own districtName values (all 'Verwaltungskreis X' except this one 'Arrondissement administratif Jura bernois' row) for consistency with cross-canton tooling. NOTHING LEFT UNCONFIRMED: all fields in BE_municipalities.json were populated directly from the official 2026 source; no nulls were needed for any of the 334 municipalities (multiplier and all three church rates were present for every single row in the source table, unlike some other cantons in this project where christ-catholic coverage is patchy).
